# Protein–protein interactions {#sec-protein-interactions}

::: {.callout-note title="From the exam description"}
Experimental and computational methods to analyse which proteins interact
and how.
:::

## Introduction

::: {.callout-warning title="To be written"}
Short introduction: binary vs. co-complex interactions; high-throughput
experimental screens and their error rates; computational prediction from
genomic context, coevolution and structure (AlphaFold-multimer); network
biology — topology, hubs, modules, and functional association networks.
:::

## Key concepts

- Experimental methods: yeast two-hybrid (binary), affinity purification–MS (co-complex), cross-linking MS, protein-fragment complementation; their biases and false-positive/negative rates
- Large interactome maps: HuRI, BioPlex; databases (STRING, IntAct, BioGRID)
- Computational prediction: genomic context, coevolution (paired MSAs), docking, deep learning (AlphaFold-multimer)
- Predicting interfaces and complex structures; evaluation (DockQ)
- Network concepts: degree distribution, scale-free networks, clustering coefficient, hubs, modules
- Functional association networks: integrating heterogeneous evidence (Bayesian integration)
- Gene regulatory networks and network inference from perturbation
- Disease networks; systems biology; metabolic modelling (flux balance analysis)

## Key papers

::: {.callout-tip}
★ = mandatory in earlier reading lists.
:::

### Reviews — start here

- ★ @guala2020 — genome-wide functional association networks.
- @barabasi2004 — network biology: understanding the cell's functional organisation.

### Experimental interactomes

- @uetz2000 — yeast two-hybrid screen of the yeast proteome.
- @gavin2002 — complexes by tandem affinity purification.
- @ho2002 — complexes by mass spectrometry.
- @vonmering2002 — comparative assessment of large-scale interaction data sets.
- ★ @rolland2014 — a proteome-scale map of the human interactome.
- @luck2020 — HuRI: a reference map of the human binary interactome.
- @huttlin2021 — BioPlex: dual proteome-scale networks.

### Computational prediction

- See genomic-context papers in @sec-protein-function.
- @burger2008 — interaction partners from sequence alignments (Bayesian method).
- @ekman2006 — what properties characterise hub proteins?
- @cong2019 — interaction networks revealed by proteome coevolution.
- @humphreys2021 — structures of core eukaryotic complexes (coevolution + AlphaFold).
- @evans2021 — AlphaFold-Multimer.
- @bryant2022 — improved prediction of protein–protein interactions using AlphaFold2.

### Networks and systems biology

- @barabasi1999 — emergence of scaling in random networks.
- @jeong2000 — large-scale organisation of metabolic networks.
- @jeong2001 — lethality and centrality in protein networks.
- @ideker2000 — discovery of regulatory interactions through perturbation.
- @ideker2001 — integrated genomic and proteomic analyses.
- @ideker2002 — discovering regulatory and signalling circuits.
- @yanai2002 — the society of genes: networks from comparative genomics.
- @rhodes2005 — probabilistic model of the human interaction network.
- @goh2007 — the human disease network.
- @lee2008 — a gene network predicts phenotypes of perturbation in *C. elegans*.
- @szklarczyk2023 — STRING.
- @orth2010 — what is flux balance analysis?
